text:
```yaml
name: CDK Compatibility Tests

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  cdk-source-connector-compatibility-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || contains(github.event.pull_request.body, '#source')
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.8'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Run source connector compatibility tests
        run: |
          tools/bin/bulk-cdk/get-certified-connectors.sh sources
          pytest tests/source_connectors/

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
        with:
          name: "Source Connector Tests"
          path: "tests/source_connectors/reports"

  cdk-destination-connector-compatibility-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || contains(github.event.pull_request.body, '#destination')
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.8'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Run destination connector compatibility tests
        run: |
          tools/bin/bulk-cdk/get-certified-connectors.sh destinations
          pytest tests/destination_connectors/

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
        with:
          name: "Destination Connector Tests"
          path: "tests/destination_connectors/reports"
```

This GitHub Actions workflow splits the original CDK compatibility test into two separate workflows, one for source connectors and one for destination connectors. Each workflow is triggered based on whether the PR body contains specific keywords (`#source` or `#destination`). The workflows run the appropriate tests and upload the test results using the `dorny/test-reporter` action.
